points.why: Never names Growth and Underinvestment; it calls the problem censoring bias plus a generic reinforcing loop.
Shows clearly that the low return of refused customers is caused by the refusal and then read as proof that demand isn't there.
Discusses the nine-month lead time and when the decision gets made, but never says capacity has to be built ahead of demand.
Recommends measuring true demand from turned-away orders, but doesn't call for holding the delivery standard fixed and even suggests rationing capacity.

pitfalls.why: Never frames the oven constraint as a fixed limit; it treats the constraint as removable by buying an oven.

notes: Suggesting tiered pricing to ration scarce capacity accepts the eroded delivery standard rather than fixing it.
